edits.name: Research helper: answers from public web pages with the link and the time fetched
edits.description: Happy can read public web pages that load without JavaScript or a login: a research helper with no memory, no accounts and no family data fetches the page, and the parent's own agent relays the answer with its link and the time it was fetched. When a page cannot be read, Happy says 'could not verify'. Nothing the helper fetches can reach the home network.
edits.example: A parent texts: 'What time does the town pool open on Saturday? Check their site.' Happy sends the hours with the link and when the page was fetched.
edits.how: First T4: one hand-off from Tony's agent to the helper with a time limit; the answer must come back in the same chat while agents still cannot see each other's sessions. Agent: a shared `research` agent from the family file, a fresh sandbox per conversation, memory search off, no accounts, tools `web_search` and `web_fetch` only, its own capped key. Each parent's agent gains `sessions_spawn` with `subagents.allowAgents: ["research"]` and `runTimeoutSeconds`; the helper's built-in finish report is the only progress message. Guardrails: both `dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork` keys unset, `tools.web.fetch.headers` empty, no fetch-provider plugin, `tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy` off, `browser.enabled: false`. One rule in the helper's AGENTS.md: give the link and the time fetched, show the page's own date when it has one, give a price or date only from a fetched page, say 'could not verify'. Four planted eval cases. Tony's agent first, Jordan's a day later. No plugin, and no rule in the house-rules plugin.

If the hand-off test (T4) fails, the only documented alternative is session visibility `tree` for the whole gateway, which changes a signed-off setting and needs Tony's yes plus a re-run of the separation check.

The home-network block rests on the fetch tool resolving and pinning the address itself, so `tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy` stays off and both private-network keys stay truly unset: an explicitly written `false` on the browser key turns hostname navigation into an allowlist and would stop the later research browser (F020).

Once the helper can fetch pages, neither the firewall nor the proxy can hold the gateway program to a list of hosts; they refuse home-network addresses and nothing more, so tool permissions, not the firewall, keep the other agents off the web.

The answer rule and the rule on what goes into a task (the town and the children's ages yes, names and the school no) are prompt rules; nothing mechanical enforces them, and the planted eval cases are the only check.

The fetch tool's home-network check covers `web_fetch` only, so host-side helpers that take a web address (the summarize wrapper, the print download, watcher scripts) need their own scheme, host and resolved-address checks.

The roadmap's one remaining leak path stays open: a parent's agent holds private chats and writes the task text for a helper that can fetch any public address. A prompt rule and planted tests guard it, and the helper's answer is treated as untrusted.

edits.example: After Happy answers 'what do I need for pancakes for six?', a parent texts 'add the flour, eggs and buttermilk to our list'. The three items appear on the shared list on both parents' phones. Later the other parent texts 'what's still on the list?' and gets the open items.
edits.how: First T9, by hand, before any code: in happy's desktop session join the list Tony names, add and tick off one item with `remindctl`, and look at both phones; then add one item with a due time and note whether a phone alerts. If the item does not arrive, try a list that Happy's account owns and shares to both parents; if that fails too, the card is dropped. Then an in-house host-side tool plugin wrapping `remindctl` with three verbs, list, add and complete, on that one list only, with no delete and no due dates, allowed on both parents' agents in the agent's tool list and the sandbox's. Reminders access is granted once by hand in the gateway's own process context. One instruction: when 'remind me' could mean a timed text or a list item, ask. No rule in the house-rules plugin: the tool's three verbs and its one list are the limit.

caveats: For a single item spoken to the phone, Siri already creates reminders with nothing to build. The bridge earns its place when the items come out of something Happy read or planned (a recipe link, the dinner plan in F033, a flyer).
If T9 fails for a list a parent owns, the fallback is a list that Happy's account owns and shares to both parents; if that fails too, the card is dropped.
The tool sets no due dates and cannot delete: an item added by mistake is ticked off, or removed on the phone. T9 notes whether a due time alerts a phone, in case a parent later asks for dated items.

edits.safety: The tool can only list, add and complete on the one list named in its configuration, so the model cannot write anywhere else or delete. An added item shows on every phone the list is shared with, so Tony confirms at execution that only the two parents share it. List text can be typed by anyone on the list, so it is treated as outside content.
